chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Arranging for the show 'Eubie' and 'Good Night, Angeline'
summary: He says he arranged numbers for the Eubie show with Roger Sequire, including a song for Louise Johnson, and 'Good Night, Angeline'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No, I didn't get a chance to see the show yet, but do you remember the numbers that you arranged for, what were they.
I got to get it. I arranged the whole show at the theatre from down in Washington. I had a boy named Roger Sequire and Roger helped me arrange the music.

No, he had the singer here, he's an arranger and he helped me arrange that music down in Washington and we come up here to the Apollo Theatre and put it on and in that show, you got to get it and then (humming) I can't ever
think of that name of that song, but that was a number that Louise Johnson, Freddie Johnson's wife she sang and it was beautiful. I arranged that.
Then he had that "Good Night, Angeline," from Jim Europe's band.
"Good Night, Angeline." Was it a ballad.
Yeah, (Singing) You know, I can remember -- oh,yeah, beautiful number.
That was one of Eubie's tunes.
